html:
SMTO-EVT-0005 — That notification is no longer available

GUID: 73cc8b30-0cc0-40a1-9f2b-009e4bd84959
Slug: notification-not-found
Domain: EVT · Subsystem: evt

What happened

  • The notification you tried to mark or dismiss isn't saved anymore, so SMTO couldn't change it. The task or schedule it was about is not affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Notifications page. The list you were looking at was out of date, perhaps changed from another window.
  2. If the notification is gone but you need its details, open the related schedule in Schedules or the related conversation directly. The work a notification points to stays in place even when the notification itself is gone.

What success looks like

  • The list loads, and Mark read or Dismiss works on the notifications shown.

If it still fails

  • If a notification that is still listed keeps showing this error, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Notification update returned 404: no retained notification record matches the requested notification_id.

What this means

  • Notification update cannot find the requested retained notification record. Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.

Why this can happen

  • Notification update cannot find the requested retained notification record.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh notifications and verify the retained item identity independently of its related task.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the client's notification list (GET /api/agent/notifications) and target a current notification_id. Updating or dismissing a notification never changes the associated task or event run.
  • Refresh notifications and select a retained item. Deleting or dismissing an item does not undo its associated task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Any edit targets an existing notification without changing associated task evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
